newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus police disperse checkpoint demonstrators.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus police disperse checkpoint demonstrators.

text.p: Police dispersed Greek Cypriots with teargas on Sunday when they tried to prevent diplomats from crossing into the Turkish-held area of the divided island through a United Nations checkpoint in the capital, police said.

Five people were taken to hospital with breathing problems when police used teargas to disperse 40 to 50 people who gathered at the U.N.-controlled Ledra Palace checkpoint in central Nicosia. They were later discharged.

Demonstrators had plans to block the checkpoint to protest what they said was the refusal of the Turkish Cypriot administration in the north of the island to allow two Maronite Christians into the southern government-controlled areas for medical treatment.
Some thumped on the bonnets of two cars belonging to diplomats of the British High Commission and the American Embassy when they appeared at the checkpoint to cross over, police said.
"They blocked off the road and some lay in the street to prevent the diplomatic cars from crossing into the occupied areas," police spokesman Glafcos Xenos told Reuters.
"We used the appropriate force to remove them and restore order," he added.

Greek Cypriots have been staging weekend demonstrations at the checkpoint for the past three months to discourage foreigners from visiting the north. Police have instructions to keep the access point open.

The island has been divided since Turkey invaded its third in 1974 in the wake of a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece. Turkish Cypriots declared a breakaway state in the north in 1983, which is recognised only by Ankara.
